newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex to provide Jalisco state service.
newsitem.headline: Telmex to provide Jalisco state service.

text.p: Former Mexican telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) was chosen by the government of western state of Jalisco to be its long distance carrier, a state official said on Friday.

"We have a little more than 1,705 phone lines in the government, of which 250 are outside lines, and all are signed up now with Telmex," local government spokesman Juan Guzman said in a telephone interview.
Estimated at $4 billion annually, Mexico's long-distance phone market opened at the beginning of the year and on March 5 in Guadalajara, Jalisco state, the nation's second-largest city.
Aside from Telmex, principal competitors for Mexican phone lines include Alestra, composed of Alfa, Visa-Bancomer and AT&T Corp, and Avantel, a venture of Banamex-Accival and MCI Communications Corp.
Guzman said the state government generates a long-distance bill of about 385,000 pesos per month.
